question: Wound healing proceeds through four sequential phases: haemostasis (minutes to hours), inflammation (1–3 days), proliferation/granulation (days to weeks), and remodelling (weeks to months/years).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The four phases are: haemostasis → inflammation (1–3 days) → proliferation (days–weeks) → remodelling (weeks–months/years). Knowing these timelines allows a forensic physician to correlate wound appearance with a plausible time of infliction — a core medicolegal skill under FM5.4.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The four phases and their typical timelines: haemostasis (immediate — minutes to hours; platelet plug and clot formation), inflammation (1–3 days; neutrophil and macrophage infiltration), proliferation (3 days to 3 weeks; fibroblast activity, granulation tissue, angiogenesis, collagen deposition), and remodelling (3 weeks to 2 years; scar maturation, collagen crosslinking). These timelines are directly applicable to medicolegal dating of wounds.
